releases.name: Gyro v0.1.0-alpha.49
releases.body:
# Gyro v0.1.0-alpha.49

Gyro Alpha 49 turns Canvas into a place to build and try things rather than read
them. A model can author an interactive UI piece as a Canvas item and you try it
in place: a Preview with responsive widths, a Code editor beside it, and
revisions that land on the same item without throwing away an unsent draft.
Provider setup stops assuming a provider, diff review reads like a diff with
real line numbers and wrapping, change counts no longer invent numbers, and
background Git reads share one deadline instead of each starting a fresh one.

## Download and install

Gyro requires macOS 14+ on Apple Silicon or Intel. Alpha app bundles use ad-hoc
code signing and are not Apple-signed or notarized. First launch requires
Apple's one-time **Open Anyway** approval.

Use the [Gyro download site](https://usegyro.io/) to choose your build, then
follow the [macOS installation guide](https://github.com/wytzeh197/Gyro/blob/main/docs/install-macos.md).

- [Apple Silicon DMG](https://github.com/wytzeh197/Gyro/releases/download/v0.1.0-alpha.49/Gyro_0.1.0-alpha.49_aarch64.dmg)
- [Intel DMG](https://github.com/wytzeh197/Gyro/releases/download/v0.1.0-alpha.49/Gyro_0.1.0-alpha.49_x64.dmg)
- [SHA256SUMS](https://github.com/wytzeh197/Gyro/releases/download/v0.1.0-alpha.49/SHA256SUMS)

Match the checksum to the exact filename you downloaded before installing.

## What changed

- **Canvas builds interfaces, not just documents.** A Canvas item can carry
  `format: "html"`: self-contained HTML, styles, and script that renders in a
  Preview with a Code editor one click away. Preview offers Fit panel, 375, 768,
  and 1280 widths plus a Restart control, so a layout can be checked at phone,
  tablet, and desktop size without leaving the chat. Revising an item reuses its
  id, an unsent local draft survives the revision and can be restored with **Use
  model version**, and the edited draft hands back to the composer with **Send
  to chat**. Text and code items stay inert, as before.
- **The preview runs where it cannot reach Gyro.** In a packaged build the
  Canvas runtime is served from its own `gyro-canvas://` origin by a dedicated
  native protocol that answers `GET /` and nothing else, under a policy with no
  same-origin, no `connect-src`, and no frames. The document arrives as one
  message from its parent, and there is deliberately no channel back: the frame
  cannot read the parent DOM, storage, or Tauri internals, and a fetch from
  inside it fails. A headless-browser check exercises interaction, revision,
  draft preservation, responsive sizing, handoff, and those isolation
  boundaries.
- **A new chat asks for a provider instead of picking one.** An unconfigured
  workspace leads to provider settings — an existing account, an API key, or a
  local model — rather than joining a provider implicitly. Connection progress
  stays visible for the whole attempt, a per-provider guard stops a second
  connect from starting while one is in flight, and a provider that reports
  itself usable offers **Use in chat**, which selects its default model for the
  current chat and opens the chat layout.
- **Diff review reads like a diff.** Comparison review shows old and new line
  numbers per line, calls its hunks *changed sections*, and offers a **Wrap
  lines** toggle for long lines. The file list shows each file's name with its
  folder beneath it, and both the list and the diff toolbar carry the file's
  change counts.
- **Counts that were measured stay measured.** An applied mutation receipt now
  supplies its file counts even when its approval row is not rendered, so the
  live, completed, and Review surfaces agree on what the turn wrote. Counts
  survive a reload, an explicitly reported zero replaces an older count, and an
  activity id reused for a different path can no longer transfer counts between
  files. Where no count was ever reported, the badge says **Line counts
  unavailable** instead of showing a zero it did not measure.
- **One chronology for the whole stream.** Provider activity, capability calls,
  and streamed assistant text now share a single order: cumulative commentary
  grows in place instead of repeating, a command keeps the position where it
  started even after it completes, a tool call landing between two tokens of a
  word no longer splits it, and text that resumes after a tool opens a new block
  so a preamble is not glued to the answer. A lost mid-turn sequence frame
  recovers after a handful of later frames instead of stalling until the turn
  ends, and reconciliation with the durable session keeps the order you watched
  arrive.
- **Bounded Git reads share one deadline.** Repository inspection runs through a
  single reader with a wall-clock budget carried across its steps: a read that
  cannot finish answers with the last known changes and says so, rather than
  leaving a stale result that looks current, and a later step cannot start with
  a fresh timeout once the budget is spent. Background status sets
  `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`, so it never refreshes the index or contends with an
  explicit stage or commit; that setting is never applied to a Git mutation.
- **Settings sheds rows that did nothing.** General, Appearance, and Advanced
  lost the fixed rows with no control behind them (startup behavior, default
  workspace, default surface, session restore, continuing sessions from the CLI,
  terminal font, reduce motion, and the local socket row), along with their
  search entries; group spacing was tightened and rounded enclosures gave way to
  thin separators.
- **DeepSeek Flash accepts images.** Image attachments now reach the
  OpenAI-compatible client for the models that support them, sent as `image_url`
  data parts under a MIME allowlist (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP). A DeepSeek model
  without image support refuses the turn and names the model to switch to
  rather than failing the request.
- **A prepared workspace is only reused when it was ready.** Cached preparation
  results are replayed only when they finished *ready* with no errors, so a
  workspace that failed to prepare is prepared again instead of being reported
  as done.

## Behavior changes and known limits

- Canvas HTML is generated content and is treated as untrusted: inline styles
  and script and `data:` images only. It cannot fetch the network, start a dev
  server, install packages, or reach Gyro's tools or workspace files. An app
  that needs dependencies or an API still belongs on a loopback dev server.
- The runtime refuses a document larger than 100,000 characters; the documented
  Canvas budget (about 12,000 characters, 16 KiB encoded) is unchanged.
- Canvas previews use the development runtime page under Vite and the dedicated
  `gyro-canvas://` origin in the packaged app. Both run the same isolated
  runtime; only the transport differs.
- An applied-receipt count is a measurement, not a diff: it reflects what a
  guarded mutation reported, and a turn that never reported counts shows no
  numbers rather than an estimate.
- A Git inspection that hits its deadline reports that it is showing the last
  known changes; retry to refresh.
- This Alpha remains ad-hoc signed and not Apple-signed or notarized.

## Upgrade and rollback

Update from Gyro or replace the application with the matching Alpha 49 DMG.
Before changing versions, quit Gyro and back up
`~/Library/Application Support/Gyro/`. To roll back, reinstall
[`v0.1.0-alpha.48.9`](https://github.com/wytzeh197/Gyro/releases/tag/v0.1.0-alpha.48.9).
This release adds an optional `html` Canvas item format and no session schema
migration; an older build ignores what it does not recognize, so sessions keep
working in both directions.

## CLI

The CLI remains version-aligned with the app.

- [Apple Silicon CLI](https://github.com/wytzeh197/Gyro/releases/download/v0.1.0-alpha.49/gyro-cli-0.1.0-alpha.49-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz)
- [Intel CLI](https://github.com/wytzeh197/Gyro/releases/download/v0.1.0-alpha.49/gyro-cli-0.1.0-alpha.49-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz)

After the validated Formula reaches the tap:

```bash
brew tap wytzeh197/tap
brew install wytzeh197/tap/gyro
# Existing CLI installations:
brew upgrade wytzeh197/tap/gyro
```

Homebrew installs the CLI only. Updater archives are signed with Gyro's updater
key, independently of the application's ad-hoc macOS signature.

releases.name: Gyro v0.1.0-alpha.48.9
releases.body:
# Gyro v0.1.0-alpha.48.9

Gyro Alpha 48.9 makes the transcript's structure trustworthy. A provider
timeline records when each piece of a turn actually arrived, so a command that
finishes late updates the item it belongs to instead of appearing at the bottom
of the conversation. A chat that needs a decision can now ask with a real choice
popup instead of a wall of prose. The browser preview follows its pane when CSS
moves it, and repository status stops showing results from a workspace you
already left.

## Download and install

Gyro requires macOS 14+ on Apple Silicon or Intel. Alpha app bundles use ad-hoc
code signing and are not Apple-signed or notarized. First launch requires
Apple's one-time **Open Anyway** approval.

Use the [Gyro download site](https://usegyro.io/) to choose your build, then
follow the [macOS installation guide](https://github.com/wytzeh197/Gyro/blob/main/docs/install-macos.md).

- [Apple Silicon DMG](https://github.com/wytzeh197/Gyro/releases/download/v0.1.0-alpha.48.9/Gyro_0.1.0-alpha.48.9_aarch64.dmg)
- [Intel DMG](https://github.com/wytzeh197/Gyro/releases/download/v0.1.0-alpha.48.9/Gyro_0.1.0-alpha.48.9_x64.dmg)
- [SHA256SUMS](https://github.com/wytzeh197/Gyro/releases/download/v0.1.0-alpha.48.9/SHA256SUMS)

Match the checksum to the exact filename you downloaded before installing.

## What changed

- **One chronology for every turn.** Provider frames and broker calls now carry
  a timeline position independent of the streaming delivery counter. A long
  command that reports back late updates the item it belongs to rather than
  inserting itself as new work at the end of the transcript, and a stream flush
  is treated as a transport boundary rather than the start of a new block.
- **Chats can ask with real choices.** When a model ends its turn with explicit
  choice questions, Gyro promotes them into a question popup above the composer
  instead of leaving them buried in prose. Options are parsed only from
  question and list structure, with code fences excluded, so a code sample or an
  ordinary paragraph never becomes a button.
- **The browser preview tracks its host.** The native child webview is now kept
  aligned to the host element's actual on-screen rectangle, so pane swaps,
  sidebar transitions, and CSS transforms no longer leave the preview behind.
  Reads are still throttled to animation frames and reported over IPC only when
  the rectangle changes.
- **Repository status stops lying after a workspace switch.** GitHub reads run
  through a refresh controller that invalidates outstanding reads when the
  workspace changes, so results from a previous workspace cannot land in the
  current one. Mutations are never retried by the controller.
- **Configurable tool-round budget.** `usageGuard.maxToolRounds` sets how many
  tool rounds a single turn may use: the default stays 512, and `0` removes the
  round budget so a long edit sweep runs until the model stops or you do. The
  window and per-call token ceilings still apply, which is what makes `0` safe
  to offer.
- **Documentation and site copy.** `docs/command-waiting.md` and
  `docs/usage-safety.md` describe the round budget and why a long wait belongs in
  one call, and the download site copy and styles were refreshed alongside them.

## Behavior changes and known limits

- A turn that exhausts its tool-round budget stops asking for tools and reports
  a checkpoint instead. Raising `usageGuard.maxToolRounds`, or setting it to
  `0`, is the supported way to let a long sweep continue.
- The question popup is derived from the last assistant message and disappears
  once you reply. A question with fewer than two or more than eight options is
  left as plain transcript text.
- The browser preview rectangle is reported from the main thread each frame; a
  host element smaller than 2×2 pixels is treated as hidden and unregisters the
  child view.
- This Alpha remains ad-hoc signed and not Apple-signed or notarized.

## Upgrade and rollback

Update from Gyro or replace the application with the matching Alpha 48.9 DMG.
Before changing versions, quit Gyro and back up
`~/Library/Application Support/Gyro/`. To roll back, reinstall
[`v0.1.0-alpha.48.8`](https://github.com/wytzeh197/Gyro/releases/tag/v0.1.0-alpha.48.8).
This release does not introduce a session schema migration; an older build
ignores capability and timeline fields it does not recognize.

## CLI

The CLI remains version-aligned with the app.

- [Apple Silicon CLI](https://github.com/wytzeh197/Gyro/releases/download/v0.1.0-alpha.48.9/gyro-cli-0.1.0-alpha.48.9-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz)
- [Intel CLI](https://github.com/wytzeh197/Gyro/releases/download/v0.1.0-alpha.48.9/gyro-cli-0.1.0-alpha.48.9-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz)

After the validated Formula reaches the tap:

```bash
brew tap wytzeh197/tap
brew install wytzeh197/tap/gyro
# Existing CLI installations:
brew upgrade wytzeh197/tap/gyro
```

Homebrew installs the CLI only. Updater archives are signed with Gyro's updater
key, independently of the application's ad-hoc macOS signature.

releases.name: Gyro v0.1.0-alpha.48.8
releases.body:
# Gyro v0.1.0-alpha.48.8

Gyro Alpha 48.8 gives the model real code intelligence and stops the browser
from taking your screen. Chats can now resolve a definition, find references, or
read a symbol's hover documentation through the same language servers the editor
uses, including in files nobody opened. Model-driven browsing runs behind the
chat instead of revealing the Browser panel over the transcript you were
reading. It also adds durable project memory, read-only Git history, a bounded
web fetch, and a research sub-agent.

## Download and install

Gyro requires macOS 14+ on Apple Silicon or Intel. Alpha app bundles use ad-hoc
code signing and are not Apple-signed or notarized. First launch requires
Apple's one-time **Open Anyway** approval.

Use the [Gyro download site](https://usegyro.io/) to choose your build, then
follow the [macOS installation guide](https://github.com/wytzeh197/Gyro/blob/main/docs/install-macos.md).

- [Apple Silicon DMG](https://github.com/wytzeh197/Gyro/releases/download/v0.1.0-alpha.48.8/Gyro_0.1.0-alpha.48.8_aarch64.dmg)
- [Intel DMG](https://github.com/wytzeh197/Gyro/releases/download/v0.1.0-alpha.48.8/Gyro_0.1.0-alpha.48.8_x64.dmg)
- [SHA256SUMS](https://github.com/wytzeh197/Gyro/releases/download/v0.1.0-alpha.48.8/SHA256SUMS)

Match the checksum to the exact filename you downloaded before installing.

## What changed

- **Code intelligence.** Chats can resolve a definition, list references, read
  hover documentation, and enumerate document symbols through the workspace's
  managed language servers. The editor and the model share one server pool, so a
  chat does not start a second copy of your language server. A cold server
  reports that it is still indexing rather than answering "not found".
- **The browser stays out of the way.** A model navigation no longer reveals the
  Browser panel by default. Gyro's browser is a native child webview, so the
  model reads a page through the agent bridge while an unrevealed browser keeps
  a full desktop viewport — in a split layout, one chat's tool call no longer
  covers the transcript you were reading in the other pane.
- **Project memory.** A chat can keep notes that survive it, stored as
  `.gyro/memory.md` in the workspace: a visible, editable, diffable file that
  travels with the project rather than a private database. Writes go through the
  same review path as any other workspace edit.
- **Read-only Git history.** `gyro_git_log`, `gyro_git_show`, and
  `gyro_git_blame` let a chat read history without touching the working tree.
  Every call builds an argument list rather than a shell string, so a revision
  or path is data and never syntax.
- **Bounded web fetch.** A chat can read a URL without opening a webview: GET
  only, text content types only, a hard byte ceiling, secret redaction, and a
  bounded redirect chain whose final URL is always reported.
- **Research sub-agent.** `gyro_research` runs one bounded, read-only provider
  turn in a fresh context and returns only its final message. It runs in Plan
  mode, so the existing read-only capability policy applies and a sub-agent
  cannot start another one. The child session is kept, so the research is
  auditable.
- **Targeted workspace edits.** Alongside whole-file proposals, a chat can
  replace an exact string inside a file it already read, instead of re-emitting
  an entire file to change three lines. Both shapes land in the same proposal
  store with the same hash guard, review, and durable decision. Chats can also
  create, rename, move, and delete files through the same root-asserted helpers
  the Workspace explorer uses.
- **Repository actions from the Environment popover.** Two coarse rows — move
  the work forward, or publish it — close the gap where the popover reported
  three uncommitted files and then left you to find the Review surface yourself.
- **Steadier provider requests.** A transient HTTP failure is retried on a short
  backoff at the request level, never by replaying an agent's already-executed
  tool loop.
- **Interface corrections.** The project hover card and edit dialog now use
  Gyro's warm neutral surfaces instead of a flat white panel, and the docked
  composer's add button lost a stray resting fill that the hero composer never
  had.

## Behavior changes and known limits

- Code intelligence depends on a language server being installed and resolvable
  for the workspace's language. Where none is available, navigation requests
  report that rather than falling back to a text search.
- The first navigation in a cold workspace can return an indexing result while
  the server warms up; retry once it has settled.
- Model navigation no longer reveals the Browser panel. Open the Browser surface
  yourself to watch a chat browse.
- Project memory is a workspace file. It is not encrypted, and it is committed
  by you like any other file — keep secrets out of it.
- `gyro_research` spends provider tokens on its own turn and blocks the parent
  tool call until it finishes.
- This Alpha remains ad-hoc signed and not Apple-signed or notarized.

## Upgrade and rollback

Update from Gyro or replace the application with the matching Alpha 48.8 DMG.
Before changing versions, quit Gyro and back up
`~/Library/Application Support/Gyro/`. To roll back, reinstall
[`v0.1.0-alpha.48.7`](https://github.com/wytzeh197/Gyro/releases/tag/v0.1.0-alpha.48.7).
This release adds new capability records and an optional workspace memory file;
it does not introduce a session schema migration, and an older build ignores
what it does not recognize.

## CLI

The CLI remains version-aligned with the app.

- [Apple Silicon CLI](https://github.com/wytzeh197/Gyro/releases/download/v0.1.0-alpha.48.8/gyro-cli-0.1.0-alpha.48.8-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz)
- [Intel CLI](https://github.com/wytzeh197/Gyro/releases/download/v0.1.0-alpha.48.8/gyro-cli-0.1.0-alpha.48.8-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz)

After the validated Formula reaches the tap:

```bash
brew tap wytzeh197/tap
brew install wytzeh197/tap/gyro
# Existing CLI installations:
brew upgrade wytzeh197/tap/gyro
```

Homebrew installs the CLI only. Updater archives are signed with Gyro's updater
key, independently of the application's ad-hoc macOS signature.

releases.name: Gyro v0.1.0-alpha.48.7
releases.body:
# Gyro v0.1.0-alpha.48.7

Gyro Alpha 48.7 adds API-key providers. DeepSeek, Mistral, OpenRouter, and any
OpenAI-compatible endpoint you define can now run a chat inside Gyro over its own
HTTPS connection, with the same tools, approvals, and streamed activity as a
provider CLI. It also makes readiness checks and chat cost reporting steadier.

## Download and install

Gyro requires macOS 14+ on Apple Silicon or Intel. Alpha app bundles use ad-hoc
code signing and are not Apple-signed or notarized. First launch requires
Apple's one-time **Open Anyway** approval.

Use the [Gyro download site](https://usegyro.io/) to choose your build, then
follow the [macOS installation guide](https://github.com/wytzeh197/Gyro/blob/main/docs/install-macos.md).

- [Apple Silicon DMG](https://github.com/wytzeh197/Gyro/releases/download/v0.1.0-alpha.48.7/Gyro_0.1.0-alpha.48.7_aarch64.dmg)
- [Intel DMG](https://github.com/wytzeh197/Gyro/releases/download/v0.1.0-alpha.48.7/Gyro_0.1.0-alpha.48.7_x64.dmg)
- [SHA256SUMS](https://github.com/wytzeh197/Gyro/releases/download/v0.1.0-alpha.48.7/SHA256SUMS)

Match the checksum to the exact filename you downloaded before installing.

## What changed

- **API-key providers.** DeepSeek, Mistral, and OpenRouter join the provider
  list, and you can add your own OpenAI-compatible endpoint in Settings with a
  base URL and key. These run over Gyro's own HTTPS client rather than a
  provider CLI, so they cross the same capability broker, approval policy,
  audit path, and stop control as every other provider.
- **Custom provider management.** Define, edit, enable, and remove your own
  endpoints in Settings, and manage the same entries from the CLI. The custom
  provider form can test the endpoint and list the models it advertises
  directly from the provider, so a definition matches what the server offers.
- **OpenRouter model list and effort.** OpenRouter carries current routed models
  and its own reasoning-effort ramp, so effort is offered only where the
  endpoint actually supports it.
- **Steadier provider readiness.** Readiness results are reused for a short
  window instead of starting a provider CLI on every check, including the
  repeated checks during sign-in. Pressing Connect, using **Test provider**, or
  finishing a sign-in always probes for real, and saving or removing a stored
  API key invalidates the previous result.
- **Visible running cost.** Providers that report per-request token counts now
  publish a running turn total as the turn works, instead of only once it
  finishes.
- **Faster launch.** Shell warm-up no longer blocks the first usable window on a
  whole-database integrity scan.
- Chat transcript attachments, provider stream ordering, and session browsing
  were hardened on the way to this release.

## Behavior changes and known limits

- An API-key provider bills the key you configure. Gyro stores it in the macOS
  Keychain when you save it there, and Gyro is the only client counting the
  tokens it sends; a provider's own dashboard remains the authority.
- Model lists for a custom endpoint reflect what the endpoint advertises when
  you fetch them. A renamed or retired model on the server side needs another
  fetch to disappear from the picker.
- A provider CLI sign-in still owns its own credentials. Choosing an API-key
  provider does not migrate or reuse a CLI login.
- Providers that do not report token counts keep showing estimated usage.
- This Alpha remains ad-hoc signed and not Apple-signed or notarized.

## Upgrade and rollback

Update from Gyro or replace the application with the matching Alpha 48.7 DMG.
Before changing versions, quit Gyro and back up
`~/Library/Application Support/Gyro/`. To roll back, reinstall
[`v0.1.0-alpha.48.6`](https://github.com/wytzeh197/Gyro/releases/tag/v0.1.0-alpha.48.6).
This release adds optional configuration fields for custom providers and does not
introduce a session schema migration; an older build ignores providers it does
not recognize.

## CLI

The CLI remains version-aligned with the app, and can manage the same custom
providers as the app.

- [Apple Silicon CLI](https://github.com/wytzeh197/Gyro/releases/download/v0.1.0-alpha.48.7/gyro-cli-0.1.0-alpha.48.7-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz)
- [Intel CLI](https://github.com/wytzeh197/Gyro/releases/download/v0.1.0-alpha.48.7/gyro-cli-0.1.0-alpha.48.7-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz)

After the validated Formula reaches the tap:

```bash
brew tap wytzeh197/tap
brew install wytzeh197/tap/gyro
# Existing CLI installations:
brew upgrade wytzeh197/tap/gyro
```

Homebrew installs the CLI only. Updater archives are signed with Gyro's updater
key, independently of the application's ad-hoc macOS signature.

releases.body:
# Gyro v0.1.0-alpha.48.6

Gyro Alpha 48.6 brings Sessions and Workspace navigation into the title bar,
adds provider API-key settings, and makes missing file-change counts explicit.

## Download and install

Gyro requires macOS 14+ on Apple Silicon or Intel. Alpha app bundles use ad-hoc
code signing and are not Apple-signed or notarized. First launch requires
Apple's one-time **Open Anyway** approval.

Use the [Gyro download site](https://usegyro.io/) to choose your build, then

- [SHA256SUMS](https://github.com/wytzeh197/Gyro/releases/download/v0.1.0-alpha.48.6/SHA256SUMS)

Match the checksum to the exact filename you downloaded before installing.

## What changed

- Sessions and Workspace navigation moves into the title bar, with improvements
  to the initial app shell and embedded surface boundaries.
- Provider settings can save and remove supported API keys in macOS Keychain,
  and provider readiness checks recognize configured keys.
- Completed-chat unread indicators stay cleared after the chat is opened.
- Chat change summaries and Review now distinguish missing line counts from
  measured zero. Incomplete totals are marked unavailable rather than borrowing
  unrelated changes from the shared working tree.

## Behavior changes and known limits

- Providers that omit file-change counts still display “Line counts unavailable.”
  This release does not reconstruct measurements missing from earlier events.
- API-key support depends on the selected provider. Provider CLI sign-in remains
  available where supported.
- This Alpha remains ad-hoc signed and not Apple-signed or notarized.

## Upgrade and rollback

releases.name: Gyro v0.1.0-alpha.48.5
releases.body:
# Gyro v0.1.0-alpha.48.5

Gyro Alpha 48.5 makes chat-owned browsing, durable working artifacts, and
long-running chat continuity more dependable. It also improves the accuracy of
context and local-model usage reporting without reducing tool or model access.

## Download and install

Gyro requires macOS 14+ on Apple Silicon or Intel. Alpha app bundles use ad-hoc

  tables, and diagrams. Browser remains the surface for interactive apps.
- Provider stream handling preserves context-usage checkpoints and settles
  activities after interrupted or out-of-order streams.

  readings remain estimated instead of being presented as measured.

  message and character bounds, so intervening tool activity no longer crowds
  out the conversation.

  once rather than duplicated in affected provider prompts.

- Browser evidence is current only when it is observed in the live browser;
  an attachment does not update after a page changes.

  attachments, or tool cycles when a provider does not report them.
- Automated checks cover the browser, canvas, stream, usage, and continuity
  contracts. Native visual acceptance and updater behavior require the release
